findings.summary: list_ready builds the onboarding overlay from an empty slice instead of the onboarding_libs parameter, while still binding onboarding_libs values positionally.
findings.mechanism: `onboarding_overlay_clause(&[])` always returns an empty string, so the generated SQL never contains the onboarding overlay's `?` placeholders. But the bind loop below (`for lib in onboarding_libs { binds.push(...) }`) still pushes one bind value per onboarding library whenever the caller passes a non-empty list. This produces either a rusqlite 'wrong number of parameters' runtime error (when `onboarding_libs` is non-empty), or if it doesn't error, misaligns the `limit` bind (bound as if in position N when the placeholder for `LIMIT ?` shifted). Functionally this also silently drops the onboarding-sample filter from `list_ready`/`skip-scan`, exactly the drift the refactor was meant to prevent — onboarding-library backlog rows that should be excluded are now enumerated.
